summary: The bench driver's Claude Code grant is not path-scoped and its documented confinement control does not exist, and checkout-mode isolation is weakened by symlinks back into the source checkout, with smaller resource-bound and credential-permission gaps.

findings.summary: The headless Claude Code grant is described as scoped, but bare Read/Edit/Write and Bash(git:*)/Bash(python3:*) are not path- or command-bounded, and the process inherits the full environment, so the stated control (confinement to the throwaway fixture) is not enforced by code.
findings.evidence: bench.py:180 CLAUDE_TOOLS = ["Read", "Edit", "Write", "Agent", "Skill", "Bash(git:*)", "Bash(python3:*)"]; bench.py:199 allowed = [*CLAUDE_TOOLS, f"Bash({skill}/bin/factory:*)"]; bench.py:184 docstring "Claude Code gets a scoped grant, never a bypass"; bench.py:439 env = dict(os.environ, FACTORY_HOME=..., FACTORY_HARNESS=...), so every inherited secret (API keys, tokens) reaches the agent's shell; the launch is at bench.py:455 with cwd=repo but no HOME override. A bare tool name in --allowedTools is not a path bound, and research.md R1 itself relies on the bare Read allow rule to read outside the grant. conformance/golden-run/claude-code.md states 'confinement to the throwaway fixture is the control', which no code enforces. The opencode launch (bench.py:186) has no grant at all and relies on rendered agent permissions that deny only edit and subagent. Rated medium and non-blocking: the run is opt-in and maintainer-driven, and fixture content is repo-controlled, so no external attacker input path is demonstrated. Under ENG-25 the authorisation boundary is still claimed where it does not exist.
findings.fix: Narrow the Bash entries to the exact commands the factory needs (for example Bash(python3 <skill>/bin/factory:*) and specific git subcommands), use path-scoped Read/Edit/Write rules limited to the output directory and skill dir, or set HOME for the launched process to the output directory as isolated_install does. Either enforce the confinement or change the docs and contract to state the exposure as an accepted risk, and apply the same restriction to the opencode leg.

findings.summary: In checkout mode the isolated skill directory symlinks repo-layer skills back to the live source checkout, so a headless run can write to the maintainer's tracked source after provenance is recorded, and those skill files are not covered by any digest.
findings.evidence: install.sh:295 link_skill "$f" "$root/$name" for f in "$src"/skills/*, and install.sh:187-188 ln -sfn "$from" "$to". Reproduced in a scratch HOME/FACTORY_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with the worktree's install.sh --harness claude-code: <scratch>/cfg/skills/bro -> /Users/tenluap/Desktop/SourceCode/Personal/claude-factory-factory/018-live-conformance/skills/bro (and the same for about 50 other skills). bench.py:366 runs isolated_install before bench.py:430 write_provenance, so the record is written before launch. The provenance digests only <out>/home/dist/<harness> (bench.py:291) and git diff HEAD of the checkout. The symlinked repo-layer skills are in neither digest, so the run's behaviour is not attributable to recorded content, and the Edit/Write grant from SEC-1 reaches the checkout's tracked files. test_bench.py test_checkout_renders_under_output_and_launches_against_it only asserts that skills/factory exists, so this is untested. Violates ENG-26 (integrity of the recorded run) and ENG-25 (trust boundary).
findings.fix: In checkout mode, copy repo-layer skills into <out>/harness-config/skills instead of symlinking them, or deny writes to the checkout path. Include the full harness-config skills tree in the provenance digest, and add a test asserting that no link in the isolated config resolves outside <out>.

findings.summary: tree_digest follows symlinks with no cycle detection and reads each file whole into memory, so a symlink cycle in the installed skill directory hangs the driver before launch.
findings.evidence: bench.py:244 os.walk(root, followlinks=True), bench.py:247-248 is_file() then file.read_bytes() (no streaming, no size bound). installed_factory (bench.py:278-283) digests the user's real skill directory inside write_provenance, which runs before the launch. Probe: a scratch skill tree containing sub/up -> .. and sub/up2 -> .. did not complete within 30 seconds under a subprocess timeout. os.walk's default onerror=None hides the resulting errors, and safe_digest catches only OSError. Triggered only by local configuration, hence low. Violates ENG-24 (bounds and timeouts).
findings.fix: Track visited realpaths or use followlinks=False, hash files in fixed-size chunks, and bound the digest with a size or time limit that records "unavailable" when exceeded.

findings.summary: Directories that hold harness credentials and session data, and the harness log, are created with the default umask (0755/0644) and retained after the run, while the golden-run procedure tells the operator to store a Claude Code login or API key in that config directory.
findings.evidence: bench.py:328-329 home.mkdir() and config.mkdir(); bench.py:361 out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False) for a user-supplied --out; bench.py:454 log.open("w") for harness.log. On this machine umask is 022 and the created harness-config directory is drwxr-xr-x. conformance/golden-run/claude-code.md tells the operator to 'Log in once with `claude` inside that config, or put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` there', and nothing removes the run tree. With Bash granted (SEC-1) and the key present in the inherited environment, the agent can print secrets into session output that persists under the config directory. Under ENG-25 secrets stay out of unprotected storage.
findings.fix: Create out, home and harness-config with mode 0o700 (os.mkdir with mode), open harness.log with 0o600, state in the procedure that credentials must be created with 0600, and either remove the disposable run tree or document its retention.

findings.summary: The headless harness launch and the checkout installer run as subprocesses with no timeout, so a hung agent or installer blocks the driver indefinitely.
findings.evidence: bench.py:455 subprocess.run(launch, cwd=repo, env=env, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT) has no timeout argument; bench.py:336-341 subprocess.run(["bash", install.sh], ..., capture_output=True, text=True) has none either. The launch line was rewritten by this diff and kept the missing bound. Under ENG-24 external processes that can run for a long time need a bound.
findings.fix: Pass a generous timeout to both subprocess.run calls, kill the process on expiry, and record the timeout as the exit status in the provenance and printed JSON.
